notes: Page 2 shows minifigure assembly (aviator helmet, head, torso, legs) plus two finished Scarab guardian minifigures for reference.

Only the dark bluish gray goggles piece (lego-30141, listed as Weapon Rifle/Gun) is in the parts list, so it is the only piece recorded. It is attached to the helmet, which is not a listed part, so it has no join to any recorded piece.
Helmet, head, torso and legs are not in the inventory and are not recorded.
The two guardian minifigures are shown as finished and are not built on this page.

Which chassis port the wheel stub axles use is a guess: b3 goes to pin-hole.1 and b4 to pin-hole.2. Each wheel centre also has a second stub axle (axle.2) that I did not connect.
The fairing's attachment point on the chassis is not clear from the drawing, so I recorded a joined edge with no ports.
Pieces b1 and earlier pages are untouched. The goggles piece (lego-30141) was not placed here.
Page 4 is step 2: a tyre is pressed onto a wheel centre, built 2x, and one wheel goes on each end of the motorcycle (front and rear).

I got page 3 wrong. Step 1 there only joins the fairing to the chassis, and the wheels first appear on this page. On page 3 I had already recorded the two wheel centres (b3, b4), the two tyres (b5, b6) and their joins to the chassis (b2). The parts list has only 2 tyres and 2 wheel centres, so I did not add them again.
b3/b5 and b4/b6 are the two wheels built here. The tyre-on-wheel joins and the wheel-to-chassis axle joins are already recorded from page 3. Page 3's fairing join (b7 to b2) is correct for step 1.
This page adds no new pieces.
Page 5 is step 3. A dark red 1x2 plate (b8) gets two trans-clear round 1x1 plates on its studs as a headlight (b9, b10). The headlight is then attached to the front of the motorcycle.

The drawing doesn't show how the headlight attaches to the front of the fairing. I assumed the plate is held in the fairing's clip (b7 clip.1) with the studs pointing forward, and left the plate-side port empty.
The 1x2 plate is dark red, matching the 2 dark red lego-3023 plates in the parts list. The other dark red plate and the dark orange one are not used yet.
Page 5 uses 2 of the 2 trans-clear round plates in the parts list.
Page 6 is a boxed sub-assembly with four steps and no model shown yet. It is probably a gun mount or accessory that gets attached to the motorcycle on a later page.
Step 1: the clip plate (b12) is clipped onto the handle end of the 1x2 handle plate (b11). Step 2: a trans-red round plate (b13) goes on the clip plate's stud.

Step 3 is unclear in the drawing. I read it as a black vertical-clip plate (b14) attached to the underside of b11, so its clip points away from the studs. I put b14's stud into b11's anti.1.1, but the exact position is a guess.
Step 4: a dark red 1x2 plate (b15) goes on top of b11's two studs. This is the second dark red lego-3023 in the parts list.
Which of the two studs on the handle plate is on the clip side is not clear, so stud.1.1 and stud.1.2 for b15 are the same kind of guess.
Page 7 has two steps. Step 4 attaches the page 6 sub-assembly (b11 to b15) to the rear of the motorcycle. Step 5 adds the red dynamite sticks (b16).
The drawing doesn't show how the sub-assembly attaches to the motorcycle, so I recorded a join between b11 and the chassis (b2) with no ports.

The dynamite is shown standing upright on the bike, next to a dark gray stick-like shape. I assumed it is held in the sub-assembly's vertical clip (b14 clip.1), but the drawing doesn't make that certain. Page 6 had put that clip on the underside of b11, so it may be on the wrong side.
I could not identify the dark gray shape beside the dynamite in step 5. I recorded no piece for it, to avoid inventing one.
Page 8 starts a new model, the pyramid / Scarab guardian scene. The inset shows the finished model. The tan 4 x 8 plate (b17) is its first piece and rests on nothing.
Step 1: a dark tan 45 degree 2 x 1 slope (b18) goes on the plate's left end. Step 2: a tan 1 x 6 brick (b19) goes beside it.

The exact stud positions are my reading of the drawing. I put the slope on row 1, columns 1-2, and the 1 x 6 brick on row 1, columns 3-8, because 2 + 6 fills the 8-stud edge. The brick could be one row further in, so treat the row as uncertain.
The slope is dark tan and the 1 x 6 brick is tan, taken from the parts list.

Page 9, step 3: the green bamboo plant (b20) goes on the back-right corner stud of the base plate (b17 stud.1.8). Step 4: the dark bluish gray 33 degree 3 x 2 slope (b21) goes in front of the 1 x 6 brick.

Correction to page 8: this page shows one row of studs behind the 1 x 6 brick (b19) and the slope (b18). So both are probably on row 2, not row 1 as I recorded. b19 should be on stud.2.3 to stud.2.8 and b18 on stud.2.1 and stud.2.2. I can't edit page 8, so the page 8 joins still say row 1.
The plant on stud.1.8 is consistent with the corrected row 2 brick, because it sits just behind the end of the brick.

The gray part in step 4 is wider than a 3 x 2 slope, and it has dark studs and two side wing shapes. These may be the two dark bluish gray double concave slopes (lego-3046a) or a rotated arrangement. Only b21 is recorded here. The stud positions (rows 3-4, columns 4-6) are my best reading.
If the 3046a slopes are what the wings are, they should appear on a later page.

Page 10, step 5: a tan 2 x 4 plate (b22) is attached to the underside of the base plate at the front, extending the base forward. The arrow comes from below, so I joined its studs to the base's anti-studs (row 4, columns 3-6).

Step 6: two dark blue pieces go on the model, then a dark tan 2 x 1 slope is lowered toward the plant end. I read the left blue piece as a 1 x 1 cheese slope (b23) and the right one as a dark blue round open-stud brick (b24). The right one sits on top of the 1 x 6 brick, directly in front of the plant. The 1 x 6 brick is assumed to be on row 2 of the base, as I noted on page 9.

Step 7 is unclear. The left tan slope looks larger and the back centre shows a stepped tan shape. I couldn't tell which pieces were added, so nothing is recorded for step 7. The positions of b26, b27 and b28 are guesses. The dark blue bricks are shown 3 studs apart with the gray round between them.

The stud positions in steps 9 and 10 are guesses. I joined the jumper to the four studs of b26. I joined each slope to the stud of one blue round brick (b27 and b28). The slopes may actually rest on other studs, such as the back wall.
With b25, b30 and b31 placed, 3 of the 7 dark tan slopes in the parts list are used so far.

b34 is joined only to the jumper's single stud (b29 stud.1.1). In the drawing it seems to sit across more of the structure, so the exact positions are a guess.

This turn adds nothing. The 7 groups are real, separate things in the booklet, and joining them would mean inventing connections that no page shows.
